samples.identification: StormAttack Windows DLL injector with Active Setup self-copy and junk trampolines; damaged embedded DLL
execution_evidence: Entry 0x402674 calls 0x401cb0 from the CRT startup. The config DWORD at VA 0x404120 is 3, selecting call 0x401900 and shell cleanup 0x401390 (0x401f8a/0x401f8f).

0x401900 gets a GUID through 0x401840 and builds an executable path under the configured Windows directory. It writes HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Active Setup\Installed Components\<GUID> StubPath using RegCreateKeyA and RegSetValueExA at 0x401a26/0x401a4b.

The active branch opens its module with fopen, fread, modifies copied-image offsets 0x6a0 and 0x3058, and writes the copy using fwrite at 0x401b26, then starts it. Those fixed offsets may no longer describe configuration fields in this modified layout; successful reconfiguration is not assumed.
0x401390 gets its own module path and 8.3 short path, reads COMSPEC, builds /c del <self> > nul, and CreateProcessA starts the deletion shell at 0x4014b8.

Alternate mode 1 extracts resource DLL/101 via 0x402460, writes it through 0x4023c0, and 0x401260 rewrites LanmanServer Parameters ServiceDLL (0x401310, 0x401320, 0x40133e). This is code capability, not the configured path.

0x401150 routes through 0x40f696 back to 0x401163; CreateProcessA starts a chosen IE/notepad/calc image. VirtualAllocEx (0x4011d1) and WriteProcessMemory (0x4011f5) transfer the DLL path. GetProcAddress resolves LoadLibraryA and CreateRemoteThread at 0x40123d uses that export with the remote path as its argument.

.htext holds genuine trampoline padding: hundreds of same-register XCHG/MOV, paired PUSH/POP and INC/DEC instructions, with jumps back into the original code. The existing suspicious self-exchange/self-move findings are justified.

Embedded PE begins at offset 0x5060. Its .rsrc and .reloc raw regions are entirely zero; .data has 1,943 nonzero bytes of 34,816 and has no executable permission. Rizin recovers no imports or exports. Surviving DDoS/HTTP/download strings do not establish an executable network payload.

No concrete Remcos, WannaCry, ransom, credential-theft, or working DDoS execution was recovered. Family identification is supported by the outer StormAttack-specific banners together with its loader and hijack implementation.

samples.identification: Unexpanded nested DTD entity declaration fragment
execution_evidence: All 53 bytes are one parameter entity declaration. Its replacement text declares a general external entity with a static HTTP URL.
There is no %eval; expansion, no &exfil; reference, no local-file entity, and no entity reference embedded in the URL. The fragment also lacks a complete XML document or DOCTYPE wrapper.

Expat with external resolution enabled records only the parameter declaration when placed in a DOCTYPE control. Adding %eval; declares the general entity without contacting its URL. Only additionally adding &exfil; calls the external resolver, which was stubbed to avoid any network request.
The name exfil and the filename xxe.xml do not establish theft. Judge BENIGN under the thin-evidence policy.
samples.marker_line: DTD entity fragment: replace XXE claims with a markup fact

samples.identification: C install function registering a recurring curl-to-Bash cron job
execution_evidence: All 110 bytes define install(void), with one system call and no main or automatic initializer. If called, system invokes a shell that lists existing jobs and appends an every-minute curl -fsSL HTTP fetch piped into Bash, installing the combined table through crontab -.
The command preserves existing jobs. Fetch and shell execution occur on the cron schedule, not during registration; no immediate network call is established by the install function itself.

No stolen source, attacker task protocol, destruction, concealment, authentication bypass, or deceptive distribution is present. The remote response is unavailable; the single-label target conveys no credible provenance. Recurring remote execution merits notable capability findings, but cannot alone convict this standalone snippet.
No obfuscation or additional hidden behavior exists in the complete source. Judge BENIGN rather than infer a missing malicious downloaded stage.

trait_changes.reason: Merge overlapping declaration-only matchers into one notable markup relationship. No invocation, read, or outbound transfer is required by these matchers. Match text includes multiline declarations; union of source/markup scopes retained. Neutral property does not inherit attack-specific testing exclusions. Preserve the former agent-skill guard on the exfiltration consumer.

Retain match conditions, scope, proximity, and playbook exclusion. Name the bounded co-occurrence rather than installation or login persistence; cron is independent of login. Notable capability does not infer unauthorized durability. Update Evooo1 consumer.

Preserve matcher and scope; cron downloading into a shell is notable and can implement legitimate update tooling. Update exact cron consumer and the miner composite that selects the old cron ancestor.
Clarify the finding as code identity; damaged resources and alternate configured modes do not prove successful service hijacking on this run.

reference_audit.exact_consumers: Updated both XML consumers, Evooo1, and cron remote-shell consumer.
reference_audit.ancestor_consumers: The miner persistence rule selects objectives/persistence/system/cron; explicitly retain the moved downloader observation as an alternative. No other actual ancestor selectors of the moved leaves were found. A local id named metadata in packaging.yaml is not a metadata directory selector.

verification.scans: atomscan and cleave facts run for every original; atomscan rerun against edited traits for every original. Local JSON scans independently confirm four hostile plus three suspicious PE traits and zero hostile/suspicious traits for each small snippet.
verification.decoded_strings: cleave strings --format json confirms the sole URL decoding layer is the GUID printf false decode; no concealed network endpoint is recovered.
